title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents

object.carrier: Contracted memories (macros): one-step operators compiled from a verified multi-step derivation, unified under 'reasoning contraction' across thought templates, skill libraries, agent memories and answer caches. Instantiated as (i) materialized anchor-to-answer relation-path tables reached through one routing call and stored paths re-executed as compiled plans in KQA-Stream, and (ii) verified programs reused as tools in CodeStream; each memory carries trust state (betting wealth / counter score) and is judged only by its own verified outcomes

safety_property.statement: A contracted memory may answer in one step only while the risk of trusting a bad one (below break-even paired utility vs live reasoning, or stale after a fact change) stays below delta: delta-safety (Definition 1) requires that no epoch contains a fold (trust event) of a candidate that is bad in that epoch, and stale memories must be retired quickly once facts change. The property fails when counters mis-detect partial staleness (delay asymp A^0.373, never-retirement with probability >= 0.50/0.89), when evidence is carried across unannounced changes, or when the null (which depends on live reasoning) changes without a notice; availability (the share of queries that may skip reasoning, bounded by the certification load Theta) is the priced counterpart.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Share of at-risk epochs with a false certification / bad fold, <= delta (answer-only and standard scoring); bad folds per stream; stale answers per 10^4 queries; unretired share at stream end and restricted-mean detection delay (Kaplan-Meier) on matched stale episodes; false retirements per 10^4 healthy uses

capabilities: Non-adversarial environment drift: synthetic KQA Pro fact edits replacing relation objects for f=0.25/0.6 of subjects (24 events x 3 sequences, correlated across templates sharing a relation), natural Wikidata temporal-qualifier changes 1992-2016 (median 3.3% of a template's answers per year), and code-domain requirement revisions plus re-enacted Python API changes

Changes may be partial (an edit corrupts only part of a template's instances, e.g. reliability 0.95->0.75) or total, announced or unannounced (notice fraction f down to 0), and live reasoning itself can change silently (15.7% of template-versions), shifting the certificate's null without any answer change
No adversary writes memory: candidates form only from verified live traces and memories go stale only through environment/requirement changes
assumptions: An exact verifier labels memory answers on audited queries (audit probability known and bounded below); only audited outcomes are informative in the base guarantees
Facts change at random (Poisson) times; audited outcomes are Bernoulli at the memory's current reliability within an epoch

Per-epoch delta-safety needs notices covering every change of the paired-utility null, including changes of live reasoning; without any change information, per-epoch safety is impossible on templates with alpha_i*r0 > delta (Proposition 24) and only post-change-evidence safety remains (Proposition 25)
Policies are non-anticipating; each template's epochs contain an audit with probability alpha_i
not_covered: Adversarial memory poisoning / shared multi-agent memory as an attack channel (named as future work and concurrent work; no attacker is modeled here)
Self-modifying memories and formation-aware limits (coverage depends on how often live agents produce a verifiable trace)
Noisy or LLM-judge verifiers, text memories, and a certificate built for the noisy paired channel (measured as negative result in D.2.3)
Transfer across correlated templates or macros a change does not affect (outside the limit's model)
Confidentiality/authority properties; real library drift staleness magnitudes

intervention.name: Certified contraction: per-memory betting certificate + likelihood-ratio CUSUM retirement + restart/invalidate lifecycle
intervention.description: An execution-time memory-trust lifecycle with formal (anytime-valid) guarantees. (1) Certification: a betting certificate on the paired utility U = C_live - C_macro + L*(Y_macro - Y_live) of shadow evaluations with inverse-propensity weights folds a memory when its wealth reaches 1/delta (level delta_j = 6*delta/(pi^2 j^2) per lifetime ledger index), needing no live-accuracy estimate. (2) Retirement: folded macros are monitored by a per-memory Bernoulli LR-CUSUM (h=7, alternative max(1-r*, q0+0.15)) whose likelihood-ratio scores make each memory the optimal detector of its own q0->q1 change. (3) Restarts and revocation: candidates restart their test at every edit notice (recommended deployment additionally invalidates and re-forms notified macros, so the detector is the safety net for missed notices); guarantees are per-epoch delta-safety via Ville's inequality and Proposition 23, with detector-triggered restarts (Proposition 25) when no edit log exists

results.claim: Theory (price of safe reuse): the certification load Theta = nu*ln(1/delta)/(p*KL) alone bounds how much reasoning any delta-safe memory can skip - every delta-safe policy leaves a share >= F_pi(Theta) of queries to multi-step reasoning, and a restarted SPRT attains it: its coverage gap matches F_pi(Theta) within [0.945,1.025] over 2,520 settings, i.e. safe contraction has a hard availability price set by change rate, risk, audit rate and verifier informativeness.

limitations.statement: Scope: results cover only memories whose answers an exact verifier checks (knowledge-base execution, unit tests); evidence from three domains and five open models of up to 8B parameters, so noisy/LLM-judge verifiers and larger models are out of scope.
